packet.model_contract: Sales are same-quarter prior-year net_sales*(1+sales_growth). Operating income=sales*(gross_margin-sga_ratio); pretax=operating+net_nonoperating_income; attributable net income=pretax*(1-effective_tax_rate)-noncontrolling_income; EPS=attributable NI/diluted shares. OCF=total net income*ocf_to_net_income; capex=sales*capex_ratio, positive outflow. Historical diluted shares may be approximated by NI attributable/diluted EPS; disclose rounding. Gross margin and SG&A are fractions of sales. Noncontrolling interest=total NI-NI attributable. Net nonoperating=interest_income+signed interest_expense+other_income. Cash conversion and capex require seasonality caveats; no debt/cash bridge or operational units/headcount forecast is supported.
packet.analysis_scope: Analyst-defined illustrative scenario model, not official company budget. Derive defensible base from eligible history; bear/bull are adverse/favorable profitability scenarios, not numeric ascending for every driver. Contract bounds are broad guardrails, not prescribed forecast estimates. All market-to-financial mappings are analyst judgments. Finance should map only financially material reference rows (latest history, same-quarter-prior-year baseline, and supporting trends), not repeat every row. No final-period outcomes are supplied. Missing detailed cash, debt, exposure, or portfolio breakdowns must be limitations, not invented observed facts. QA evaluates a transparent illustrative model; uncertainty alone is not an error, but unsupported claims of certainty are.

history_control_assumptions.basis: Reported growth was approximately 2% in prior-year Q4, 3% in FY2026 Q1 and 1% in Q2, with Q2 organic growth flat. Base assumes modest growth between the seasonal reference and latest reading; bear assumes contraction and bull a recovery above recent growth. These are total reported-growth assumptions, without separately adding historical FX, price or mix contributions.

Prior-year Q4 gross margin was approximately 49.11%, versus 51.37% and 51.22% in recent Q1 and Q2. Base allows partial retention of recent margins while respecting the lower Q4 seasonal reference. Bear assumes deterioration below prior-year Q4; bull assumes recent margin strength persists. Cost and mix mechanisms are illustrative judgments without supplied market evidence.

Prior-year Q4 SG&A/sales was approximately 28.26%, versus 25.21% in recent Q1 and 27.05% in Q2. Base stays close to the seasonal Q4 reference rather than extrapolating Q1's low ratio. Bear assumes expense pressure and weaker sales absorption; bull assumes improved expense efficiency. Higher ratios are adverse.

Contract-defined historical component totals were 166 in prior-year Q4, 179 in recent Q1 and 55 in Q2. Base rounds to a cautious positive contribution between the latest and seasonal references; bear allows a net expense and bull a stronger positive contribution. No interest-rate, debt-balance or exceptional-gain forecast is asserted.

Reported rates were 19.8% in prior-year Q4, 20.8% in recent Q1 and 20.1% in Q2. Base rounds near the seasonal and latest references; bear assumes a higher tax burden and bull a lower burden, near the supplied FY2025 Q3 rate of 18.6%. No specific tax benefit or jurisdictional mix change is forecast.

Total less attributable net income gives 11 in prior-year Q4, 31 in recent Q1 and 12 in Q2. Base follows the latest reading and seasonal reference. Bear assumes a larger deduction from total earnings, near Q1; bull assumes a modestly smaller deduction. Ownership and subsidiary earnings details are unavailable.

Attributable earnings divided by rounded diluted EPS imply approximately 2442.6 million shares in prior-year Q4 and 2426.4 million in latest Q2. Base assumes only a modest further decline; bear allows the denominator to remain near the prior-year level and bull assumes a larger decline. Lower shares favor EPS; none of these values establishes an observed or authorized repurchase program.

Quarterly OCF/total net income was approximately 1.375 in prior-year Q4 and 1.148 in latest Q2. Base gives greater weight to the same-quarter seasonal reference but discounts its repeatability. Bear assumes weaker cash conversion; bull assumes stronger conversion above prior-year Q4. Working-capital timing is uncertain and these ratios are not annualized.

Positive capex outflow/sales was approximately 4.77% in prior-year Q4 and 5.25% in latest Q2. Base lies between these references. Bear assumes greater spending intensity and bull lower near-term cash outflow. Capital-spending timing is seasonal; no project pipeline or deferred-investment claim is supported.

packet.comparison_instruction: Use this frozen history-only control as the counterfactual. Explain incremental changes driven by eligible market evidence; leave unrelated drivers unchanged unless a specific justified correction is necessary. Market research uncertainty can widen scenarios without forcing base changes.
